edges.mechanism: Betaine remethylates homocysteine to methionine; in CBS deficiency methionine cannot be cleared via transsulfuration and can reach 1,000-3,000 umol/L, with reported cerebral edema. FDA label: monitor methionine, keep <1,000 umol/L via diet and betaine dose reduction.
edges.evidence: FDA label warning plus case reports/review of 19 patients and a crossover RCT suggesting doses >100 mg/kg/day may harm hypermethioninemic patients

edges.mechanism: Betaine at >=4 g/d raises total and LDL cholesterol (LDL +0.36 mmol/L at 6 g/d; pooled LDL +10.3 mg/dL), potentially offsetting any homocysteine benefit; effect not seen at <4 g/d.
edges.evidence: SR/MA of RCTs and pooled RCT data; EFSA used the 4 g/d LDL effect as its reference point

edges.mechanism: True physiological rise in LDL/total cholesterol with gram-dose betaine (evident within 2 weeks at 6 g/d).
Betaine-driven remethylation raises plasma methionine (MD +2.06 umol/L in healthy adults; large rises in CBS deficiency).
edges.evidence: SR/MA in healthy adults; label and case series in CBS deficiency

edges.mechanism: Betaine lowers fasting tHcy (about -1.2 umol/L; 12-20% at 1.5-6 g/d) and blunts the post-methionine-load rise; interpret tHcy results with this in mind.
DMG is the direct BHMT product; it rose 16.5-fold with ~10 g/d in prediabetes. Elevated DMG is an observational mortality risk marker in CHD (causality unknown).
Betaine is a TMAO precursor; supplementation produced a non-significant TMAO rise; betaine and TMAO were CVD risk predictors in metabolomics cohorts.
edges.evidence: Crossover RCT (P=.053) and metabolomics cohort; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Folate-dependent methionine synthase and betaine-dependent BHMT are parallel remethylation routes; folic acid raises plasma betaine up to 15%, and betaine-homocysteine associations are strongest at low folate status. Folic acid lowers fasting Hcy without raising lipids.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic RCT/cohort data; no direct 5-MTHF plus betaine trial

edges.mechanism: B12 is the methionine synthase cofactor; BHMT provides a B12-independent remethylation route. Betaine is combined with hydroxocobalamin in cobalamin defects; low-dose B vitamins plus 1 g betaine lowered Hcy 10.1%.
edges.evidence: Guideline (inborn errors) and combination RCT that cannot isolate betaine

edges.mechanism: Same complementary remethylation pathways as for Vitamin B12; no trial specific to methylcobalamin plus betaine.
B6 drives transsulfuration (CBS/CGL) while betaine drives remethylation; B6 deficiency raises post-load Hcy, and betaine added to folate+pyridoxine lowered post-load Hcy a further 18% in CKD.
Combined folate/B6/B12 plus betaine lowered Hcy; methyl-donor co-supplementation (betaine HCl + B vitamins) prevented guanidinoacetate-induced hyperhomocysteinemia.
Metformin lowers B12 and raises Hcy (+2.02 umol/L without B-vitamin co-supplementation). Betaine's BHMT pathway could theoretically offset the Hcy rise, but no co-administration study exists.
edges.evidence: RCTs and MA for metformin effects; betaine interaction is theoretical

edges.mechanism: Bezafibrate causes abnormal urinary betaine loss associated with higher plasma homocysteine.
Betaine >=4 g/d raises LDL, which may partly counter lipid-lowering goals (inferred; no interaction study).

Choline donors are oxidized to betaine; supplemental choline raises plasma betaine, lowers Hcy and (as phosphatidylcholine) raised TG; choline and betaine are both TMAO precursors. Data are for choline bitartrate/phosphatidylcholine, not Alpha-GPC specifically.
edges.evidence: RCTs of other choline forms; extrapolated

edges.mechanism: T-allele carriers had larger serum betaine increases after supplementation; no genotype x dose interaction for performance; no genotype-guided clinical benefit established.
Betaine is guideline first-line and an FDA-labelled indication; requires specialist dosing and monitoring of tHcy/methionine.
Betaine did not lower fasting Hcy beyond folate in dialysis/CRF but lowered post-load Hcy; DMG accumulates; lipids rose slightly.
Limited human data; label reports no identified drug-associated risk from case reports; no animal reproduction studies.
